習.meaning: A penguin signs up for night school. Every evening she dips two <part>feathers</part> in a pot of <part>white</part> paint and copies the teacher's letters onto the blackboard, wobble by wobble. By the end of term she can write her own name. She's starting to <kanji>learn</kanji>.
習.on: Her homework is to write the whole alphabet on the sole of a <sound>shoe</sound>.
習.kun: '<sound>Nah</sound>, try again,' says the teacher, so she practises until the whole class cheers '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

編.meaning: Overnight a spider takes down every note from the village <part>notice board</part>, lost cats, cake sales, a missing wig, and stitches them together with its own <part>thread</part>. In the morning a fat book hangs on the board: the whole year's <kanji>compilation</kanji>.
編.on: The first reader is a nosy <sound>hen</sound>, pecking through the pages for gossip.
編.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' clucks the hen, and asks the spider to knit her a scarf as well.

庁.meaning: On a quiet <part>street</part> stands a tiny garden <part>shed</part> with a brass plate on the door. Inside, one clerk stamps forms for the whole country: dog licences, rocket permits, moon parking. It's the national <kanji>agency</kanji> for everything.
庁.on: The clerk wears a tight lace <sound>cho</sound>ker that squeaks every time she brings the stamp down.
庁.kun: Out in the back <sound>ya</sound>rd, a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo runs a little <sound>sho</sound>p selling the blank forms.

損.meaning: An office <part>employee</part> uses a ship's <part>anchor</part> as a paperweight. When the fan starts blowing, he slams it down hard: it crashes through his desk, three floors and the boss's aquarium. The boss stands in the puddle and adds up the <kanji>damage</kanji>.
損.on: A soggy <sound>som</sound>brero floats up out of the broken aquarium.
損.kun: His <sound>so</sound>cks are soaked, so he hangs them to dry on a <sound>co</sound>t in the basement.

訳.meaning: A tailor holds his <part>measure</part> up against a foreign king's <part>speech</part>, snips it into pieces and stitches the words back together in a new language, each one cut to fit. At last the crowd understands. He knows how to <kanji>translate</kanji>.
訳.on: As thanks, the king hands him a spiky <sound>yuc</sound>ca plant in a gold pot.
訳.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' wails the king's baby, who wants to know why the tailor brought <sound>ke</sound>tchup to a palace.

策.meaning: A panda wants the berries hidden inside a <part>thorn bush</part>. It lashes <part>bamboo</part> canes into a long grabber with a fork on the end, creeps up at midnight in a fake moustache and fishes them out one by one. It's a cunning <kanji>scheme</kanji>.
策.on: For dessert it sneaks into the garden centre and steals a fat <sound>suc</sound>culent too.

略.meaning: A painter is paid to paint <part>each</part> <part>rice field</part> in the valley, all two hundred of them. After three, she paints one big green square, writes 'etc.' underneath and goes for lunch. Nobody ever notices the <kanji>omission</kanji>.
略.on: Over lunch she sings an a<sound>ria</sound>, the 'ree-ah' squeezed into one quick note, and a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo joins in.
略.kun: She sips something <sound>ho</sound>t from a <sound>bo</sound>ttle and calls the job finished, or almost.
